meaning: Research priorities, not endorsements, alpha reports or verified marginal donation offers.

selection.name: Harm Reduction Services
selection.reason: Strong, immediate overdose/infection pathway in a local high-risk population; more geographically concentrated than national distribution groups.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Show donation-sensitive outreach capacity after free state naloxone/syringe supplies and public contracts; confirm current unrestricted recipient.

selection.name: Operation Access
selection.reason: Donated specialty/surgical capacity gives a clearer route from coordination spending to otherwise-unavailable treatment than broad reimbursed clinics.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Obtain marginal completed-case mix, volunteer/operating-room constraint and counterfactual access; exclude donated-care sticker value.

selection.name: Champions for Health
selection.reason: SanDiego donated specialty care plus vaccination creates plausible low-cost clinical leverage; selected to compare whole-portfolio efficiency with Operation Access.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Separate all-program spending from Project Access; establish donation-sensitive procedures and vaccine coverage gaps, not just provider donations.

selection.name: End Overdose
selection.reason: Direct life-preserving mechanism and existing report provide a useful national-vs-local harm-reduction comparator despite CA dilution.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Estimate CA share of marginal unrestricted activity, kit substitution and use by otherwise-unprotected people; reuse prior model without inheriting national geography.

selection.name: Homeless Health Care Los Angeles
selection.reason: Local overdose/wound care reaches unusually high-risk people outside ordinary clinics; potentially more donation-sensitive than a large FQHC.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Trace unrestricted spending across street care, housing and broad therapies; verify incremental treatment and no reimbursed-care substitution.

selection.name: Western Center on Law & Poverty
selection.reason: California-focused legal enforcement can unlock existing healthcare/benefit entitlements at population scale.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Find specific live donation-sensitive cases/rule changes, counterfactual legal success and health effect; allocate coalition credit conservatively.

selection.name: Youth ALIVE!
selection.reason: Targeted recurrent-violence prevention has large lifetime upside and existing local research to challenge rather than recreate.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Reuse accepted report evidence; test donor-sensitive expansion, selection bias and secular violence trends across entire portfolio.

selection.name: Community Water Center
selection.reason: Targeted unsafe-water access combines measurable exposure with public-infrastructure leverage, stronger health linkage than generic climate organizing.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Identify marginal households, contaminants/doses and actual exposure reduction; separate already-financed water/infra and policy attribution.

selection.name: Worksafe
selection.reason: Occupational hazard enforcement offers repeated injury/exposure prevention across workplaces with a relatively concrete causal chain.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Test whether donations change enforcement/repairs beyond State Bar support; settlement money and legal wins alone do not establish safer work.

selection.name: Coalition for Clean Air
selection.reason: California pollution implementation offers population scale and a legacy comparison anchor; prioritize marginal enforcement over gross regulatory benefits.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Reuse current report and finite implementation model; verify live CA exposure reduction, additional funding capacity and coalition contribution.

selection.name: Disability Rights California
selection.reason: In-state legal support for medically vulnerable residents may preserve high-benefit home/health services across many people.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Measure donation-sensitive work beyond statutory public funding; assess institutional/community-care effects including harms and substitution.

selection.name: California Pan-Ethnic Health Network
selection.reason: California health-access policy concentration gives a credible statewide treatment-access pathway compared with broader policy organizations.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Locate a specific live administrative barrier that can be changed; verify treatment uptake and distinct contribution amid overlapping coalitions.

selection.name: Didi Hirsch Mental Health Services
selection.reason: Suicide prevention and treatment for severe distress create substantial upside; multiple CA clinical sites and local service evidence improve readiness.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Determine marginal CA service mix and private-gift role versus public reimbursement; do not map resolved calls directly to suicides prevented.

selection.name: California Dental Association Foundation
selection.reason: Volunteer dental treatment can relieve severe untreated pain/infection at modest coordination cost; distinct recipient already source-linked.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Verify donation allocation to incremental completed treatment versus dentist wellness/student/workforce support and establish benefit duration.

selection.name: National Health Law Program
selection.reason: Dedicated California health-law activity could remove recurring coverage/treatment barriers at statewide scale.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Apportion national unrestricted allocation to CA; identify unique legal contribution and completed effective care, avoiding HCA co-counsel double credit.

selection.name: Walk San Francisco
selection.reason: Specific speed and intersection changes offer a more testable injury pathway than broad transport/climate agendas.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Establish current recipient and additional influence on implemented designs/enforcement; model displaced traffic and agency action absent donation.

selection.name: Nourish California
selection.reason: Focused nutrition-policy work may unlock publicly financed benefits more efficiently than incremental donated food logistics.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Show a feasible marginal policy/enrollment change, actual nutrition improvement and health translation rather than benefit-dollar totals.

selection.name: The Children's Partnership
selection.reason: Child coverage retention and mental-health access have long-lived upside and a focused California policy remit.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Verify measured treatment/retention changes and distinct contribution versus Children Now/CPEHN; avoid converting messaging reach into health.

selection.name: California School-Based Health Alliance
selection.reason: Technical assistance can enable durable access to school medical/mental services for underserved children; more scalable than one-off awareness.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Show additional functioning clinics or more effective care because of new funds; member-clinic outcomes cannot all accrue to the alliance.

selection.name: Breathe Southern California
selection.reason: Poorly controlled asthma is a concrete treatable burden; useful test of prevention access rather than generic broad-clinic subsidy.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Determine whether gifts expand effective asthma management beyond Medi-Cal payment and whether other respiratory/environmental programs dilute margin.

selection.name: Center for Independent Living
selection.reason: Device repair and personal-support access may restore substantial daily function cheaply; clearer local delivery than umbrella advocacy.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Measure actual incremental repairs/support, functional duration and substitution by insurance or CFILC-funded programs across whole recipient.

selection.name: Comite Civico del Valle
selection.reason: Imperial Valley asthma/heat/exposure programs combine concentrated vulnerability and concrete preventable illness.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Separate effective direct prevention from broad energy/litigation portfolio; quantify current unmet activity and any negative policy tradeoffs.

selection.name: Essential Access Health
selection.reason: Provider networks may bridge high-value reproductive preventive-care access gaps across California.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Verify truly unfunded delivery/implementation versus federal pass-throughs; apportion Hawaii/national work and measure clinical—not ideological or spending—outcomes.

selection.name: California YIMBY Education Fund
selection.reason: A small chance of incremental broad housing implementation has potentially large CA upside; warrants one explicit long-chain high-upside test.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Resolve Education Fund-specific education/research influence, not c4/PAC lobbying; test construction-to-housing-stability-to-health chain and opportunity costs.

selection.name: Vision To Learn
selection.reason: Straightforward school vision correction and source-confirmed recipient provide a testable low-cost clinical comparator to advocacy bets.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Measure CA marginal allocation, consistent glasses wear/replacement and health utility (not education scores alone); reuse existing report.

selection.name: National Center for Healthy Housing
selection.reason: Prioritize scalable lead/asthma implementation leverage over generic housing advocacy; full portfolio remains to be costed.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Attribution to changed policy, implementation probability and clinical QALY conversion; lead-related earnings are not automatically QALYs.

selection.name: Legal Action Center
selection.reason: Prioritize enforceable addiction and mental-health access rights; more direct health-care linkage than broad economic-rights advocacy.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Legal wins/coverage entitlements require actual effective treatment uptake; coalition contribution and non-health portfolio share can dominate.

selection.name: National Health Law Program
selection.reason: Prioritize healthcare-specific legal enforcement and implementation; retained coverage must lead to effective additional care.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Litigation or enrollment changes must cause additional effective treatment; coalition credit and court reversals matter.

selection.name: Center for Science in the Public Interest
selection.reason: Prioritize population food standards and reformulation potential; implementation and dietary substitution must survive scrutiny.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Policy implementation, diet substitution, industry adaptation and actual morbidity changes must be established.

selection.name: Kids and Car Safety
selection.reason: Prioritize focused child vehicle-safety regulation with durable fleet-wide effects; burden and remaining opportunity cap upside.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Small absolute mortality burden, manufacturers' independent progress and uncertain marginal policy contribution may erase apparent upside.

selection.name: Institute for Safer Trucking
selection.reason: Prioritize focused truck-safety regulation and fleet effects; implementation timing and independent manufacturer progress may defeat hypothesis.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Reject if rules would occur without the organization or advocated measures fail implementation or safety tests.

selection.name: American Nonsmokers' Rights Foundation
selection.reason: Prioritize charitable smoke-free implementation resources with focused US exposure pathway; exclude lobbying affiliate output.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Remaining policy opportunities may be difficult; historical national trends are not charity-attributable effects.

selection.name: Immunize.org
selection.reason: Prioritize clinical vaccination practice support with potentially low-cost repeated use; prove changed timely vaccination, not downloads.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Tools downloaded or professionals reached do not establish additional timely vaccination.

selection.name: Shatterproof
selection.reason: Prioritize addiction-treatment quality and payer implementation; effective medication uptake is the critical bridge to health.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Provider listings and insurer endorsement do not prove treatment completion, evidence-based medication uptake or mortality effects.

selection.name: Green & Healthy Homes Initiative
selection.reason: Prioritize an implementer with a direct exposure-remediation pathway; use full repairs and counterfactual public funding.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Before/after health claims lack a clear counterfactual; repairs can be expensive and public funds may substitute.

selection.name: Earthjustice
selection.reason: Prioritize population pollution litigation upside, but legal contribution and domestic share must be small defensible fractions.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Do not credit an entire regulation to one litigant; reversals, delays, substitution and current marginal funding matter.

selection.name: End Overdose
selection.reason: Selected after removing HBBF sponsor-scope hold: direct naloxone availability and trained witnesses provide a concrete severe-harm pathway missing from the prior shortlist. Prioritize testing targeting, supply substitution and causal rescue benefit.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Kits and training may reach low-risk people, substitute publicly supplied naloxone, remain unused or arrive too late. Distribution and reported reversals cannot be treated as incremental deaths averted; survivor follow-up and competing mortality matter.

selection.name: US Alcohol Policy Alliance
selection.reason: Prioritize population alcohol-policy implementation, a distinct prevention mechanism; failed or nonadditional policy adoption can erase upside.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Reject if supported policies are not adopted, lack enforcement or are not causally additional.

selection.name: Dental Lifeline Network
selection.reason: Prioritize comprehensive volunteer dental care for medically vulnerable patients; evaluate durable pain/function benefits and fully cost coordination.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Reject if volunteer care displaces other care, benefits are short-lived or medical clearance would occur anyway.

selection.name: Remote Area Medical
selection.reason: Prioritize tangible vision correction and dental pain relief using volunteer delivery; demand durability and follow-up rather than retail-value claims.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Short episodic care may lack follow-up; volunteer and equipment contributions plus outside-care substitution matter.

selection.name: Rx Outreach
selection.reason: Prioritize low-cost chronic medication access with an observable dispensing-to-adherence pathway; earned revenue and market alternatives must be reconciled.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Must show additional adherence rather than switching from similarly priced pharmacy options.

selection.name: The Headstrong Project
selection.reason: Prioritize a direct trauma-treatment pathway with patient outcomes that can be checked; include dropout, relapse and available alternatives.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Completer-only symptom results can overstate effect; account for dropout, relapse, VA/private-care alternatives and therapist cost.

selection.name: Help America Hear

selection.decisiveQuestion: Reject if devices go unused or affordable alternatives would meet the same need.

selection.name: Surgery on Sunday

selection.decisiveQuestion: Reject if case mix is low-benefit, complications offset gains or hospital charity would provide equivalent care.

selection.name: Cribs for Kids

selection.decisiveQuestion: No extra clinically indicated treatment beyond alternate clinics/reimbursement; screening overdiagnosis, low adherence, clinical harm or full recipient cost makes incremental benefit negligible/negative.

selection.name: MetroWest Free Medical Program
selection.reason: Volunteer clinical care and explicit coordinator/interpreter funding make an uninsured-access margin unusually legible; compare FQHC referral alternatives.
selection.decisiveQuestion: No extra clinically indicated treatment beyond alternate clinics/reimbursement; screening overdiagnosis, low adherence, clinical harm or full recipient cost makes incremental benefit negligible/negative.

selection.name: Samaritans Inc.
selection.reason: Volunteer-supported crisis access may act quickly on high-risk distress; require local routing, counterfactual 988 coverage and intervention-harm checks.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Contacts fail to create incremental appropriate care or durable symptom/safety improvement; displacement of 988 providers, insurance-supported capacity, unwanted emergency interventions or treatment harms erase gains.

selection.name: Health Law Advocates
selection.reason: Legal work directly secures mental-health and coverage access; case-to-treatment follow-through can support a finite partial-health model.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Legal/enrollment success does not change appropriate treatment, housing safety or health; other counsel or automatic benefit access would substitute; policy is inevitable or harmful once fiscal/administrative effects are included.

selection.name: HomeStart
selection.reason: Preventing eviction may avert prolonged homelessness with a shorter intervention than shelter construction; quantify true prevention and public-assistance displacement.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Assistance changes neither homelessness duration nor durable symptoms/safety relative to legal aid, public rent assistance and alternate shelter; housing supply constraints or displacement dominate.

selection.name: Community Servings
selection.reason: Medically tailored meals offer an explicit diagnosis-specific nutrition mechanism; examine causal study quality, paid contracts and full meal-resource costs.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Food displaces purchases/other assistance without improving nutrition, disease control or insecurity; referral selection confounds observed medical utilization; delivery and donated-food resource costs offset gains.

selection.name: Fenway Health
selection.reason: Differentiated HIV/LGBTQ access creates a plausible underserved-care advantage; test whole-gift allocation and national research/nonlocal reach.
selection.decisiveQuestion: No extra clinically indicated treatment beyond alternate clinics/reimbursement; screening overdiagnosis, low adherence, clinical harm or full recipient cost makes incremental benefit negligible/negative.

selection.name: Casa Esperanza
selection.reason: Bilingual integrated addiction/behavioral care may reach people conventional services miss; compare retention and reimbursement with Gavin/Victory.
selection.decisiveQuestion: No additional treatment retention, overdose response or risk reduction after public funding, other providers and natural recovery; residential costs or coercive/ineffective treatment may outweigh finite health gains.

selection.name: The Dimock Center
selection.reason: Roxbury addiction and integrated health pathways are direct; reconcile umbrella/clinical entities and avoid narrow program-cost cherry-picking.
selection.decisiveQuestion: No extra clinically indicated treatment beyond alternate clinics/reimbursement; screening overdiagnosis, low adherence, clinical harm or full recipient cost makes incremental benefit negligible/negative.

selection.name: Eastern Massachusetts Abortion Fund
selection.reason: Prospective financial/logistical barriers are explicitly addressed; quantify other coverage/funds, local residency and actual care changed.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Care would have occurred without gifts, funding displaces insurance/other funds, or barriers are nonfinancial; resident-local health/welfare gain fails to justify all resources and intervention harms.

selection.name: Boston Area Rape Crisis Center
selection.reason: Focused sexual-violence counseling and medical advocacy give a tractable trauma-health mechanism, rather than assuming all outreach averts assaults.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Safety planning/counseling does not reduce trauma symptoms or repeat violence beyond alternatives; displacement, retaliation, coercive responses or nonlocal service costs erase the gain.

selection.name: The Brookline Center for Community Mental Health
selection.reason: Focused reduced-fee clinical care and early-psychosis programs merit direct finite symptom/access modeling, with actual private-gift margin.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Contacts fail to create incremental appropriate care or durable symptom/safety improvement; displacement of 988 providers, insurance-supported capacity, unwanted emergency interventions or treatment harms erase gains.

selection.name: Health Care For All
selection.reason: Navigation may unlock treatment while policy can affect many eligible residents; separate direct and systemic channels and transfers.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Legal/enrollment success does not change appropriate treatment, housing safety or health; other counsel or automatic benefit access would substitute; policy is inevitable or harmful once fiscal/administrative effects are included.

selection.name: Project Bread
selection.reason: Enrollment and policy leverage may dominate bulk food distribution for some households; explicitly model displacement and nutrition/health translation.
selection.decisiveQuestion: Food displaces purchases/other assistance without improving nutrition, disease control or insecurity; referral selection confounds observed medical utilization; delivery and donated-food resource costs offset gains.

selection.name: Victory Programs

selection.decisiveQuestion: No additional treatment retention, overdose response or risk reduction after public funding, other providers and natural recovery; residential costs or coercive/ineffective treatment may outweigh finite health gains.

selection.decisiveQuestion: Assistance changes neither homelessness duration nor durable symptoms/safety relative to legal aid, public rent assistance and alternate shelter; housing supply constraints or displacement dominate.

selection.decisiveQuestion: No additional treatment retention, overdose response or risk reduction after public funding, other providers and natural recovery; residential costs or coercive/ineffective treatment may outweigh finite health gains.

selection.name: Health Imperatives

selection.decisiveQuestion: Care would have occurred without gifts, funding displaces insurance/other funds, or barriers are nonfinancial; resident-local health/welfare gain fails to justify all resources and intervention harms.

selection.decisiveQuestion: Legal/enrollment success does not change appropriate treatment, housing safety or health; other counsel or automatic benefit access would substitute; policy is inevitable or harmful once fiscal/administrative effects are included.
